newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: LME zinc may probe US$1,600, but correction seen.
newsitem.headline: LME zinc may probe US$1,600, but correction seen.

text.p: London Metal Exchange (LME) zinc prices are seen hitting a fresh seven-year peak above stiff resistance at US$1,600 a tonne later on Friday, but the metal will be vulnerable to bouts of profit-taking, dealers said.
"From the way it looks, the trend is going to be $1,600 for zinc," one dealer said. "But we feel a correction will come in August and zinc will come down to below $1,500 (a tonne)."
Zinc powered higher on Thursday due to tightness in key spreads as the market focused on reports that Chinese smelters were heavily short.
Three-month zinc was indicated late in London on Thursday at $1,585/90 a tonne. A metal house in Singapore quoted zinc a touch firmer at around $1,588/93 a tonne at 0230 GMT on Friday.
"It's going to hit $1,600 earlier than expected," a dealer said, adding though that he felt it may happen early next week.
LME broker Rudolf Wolff said of zinc in its daily review that while it remained wary of "a corrective pullback...any such dips are likely to provide an opportunity to go long."
Wolff said initial resistance will be found at $1,580, "with a primary target of $1,600."
"I think the topside for zinc is $1,620. Then profit-taking should come in," a dealer said.
But Far East dealers generally said they were increasingly sceptical that the fundamental situation in the market justified the steep rise in zinc prices.
"No, the price is not fundamentally justified. I don't really see any buying at this time. If you look at the stocks in Singapore, I don't see any stuff going out," one said.
"The funds are just buying it up. I don't think they'll liquidate at this time," another trader said.
The volume of zinc stocks in Singapore reached 42,295 tonnes on Thursday, up from the previous day's 41,800 tonnes.
A Japanese trader said zinc supplies worldwide will tighten towards the end of the year and into 1998 but that prices were not now reflective of current supply and demand.
"I think the price is artificial. I don't think it is the right price for zinc. The right price should be around $1,400 to $1,450 (a tonne)," he said.
Copper prices, on the other hand, are seen steady to slightly firmer later on Friday after the backwardation narrowed on the LME to $45/$50 a tonne from $270 last week.
"Copper should increase a little bit, but not much," a Japanese dealer said.
"With the technical indicators showing signs of strengthening coupled with the close on the highs, look for initial challenges of $2,300, then to $2,350," Wolff said.
Three-month copper was quoted by one metal house at 0230 GMT at around $2,319/24 a tonne against the late quote on the LME of $2,317/25 a tonne on Thursday.
